title: Localized top Chern class
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $F$ be a rank-$r$ vector bundle on $T$, let $s$ be a regular
section, and write $i:Z(s)\hookrightarrow T$. There is a canonical
morphism

$$
c_r(F,s):i_*\Lambda_{Z(s)}\longrightarrow\Lambda_T(r)[2r]
$$

with the following properties:

1. *(L1)* for $r=1$ it is the localized Kummer class of the
Cartier divisor of $s$ (of [lem-pur-divisor-class]);
1. *(L2)* it commutes with base change whenever the
pulled-back section is still regular, in particular with
arbitrary base change for the tautological section on the total
space of a vector bundle;
1. *(L3)* for a transverse direct sum of sections it is the
cup product of the two localized classes;
1. *(L4)* after forgetting support it is $c_r(F)$.

Its construction uses only ordinary cohomology-with-support groups
and the projective-bundle formula.

proof.text: For $r=0$, the section is empty, $Z(s)=T$, and take $c_0(F,s)=\operatorname{id}_{A_T}$. Its support-forgetting image is $c_0(F)=1$, and pullback and products preserve the unit. Henceforth $r>0$. Write supported classes as morphisms using [lem-pur-supported-hom]. For the complete flag bundle [def-pur-complete-flag-bundle], [lem-pur-flag-pullback-injective] gives the supported splitting principle. In particular it is injective with full support, which will detect the ordinary equality in (L4).

Let $\pi:E=E(F)\to T$ be the total space and $z:T\hookrightarrow E$ its zero section [def-pur-vector-bundle-zero-section]. On a trivializing affine $U\subseteq T$, this is the pair $(\mathbf A^r_U,U)$ with ideal $(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$. Affine space is smooth of dimension $r$ over $U$, and $U\to U$ is smooth of dimension zero [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]. The coordinates are successive nonzerodivisors: multiplication by a polynomial variable is injective over any coefficient ring, and quotienting by it removes that variable. The local rings are Noetherian (finite type over the field). Iterating [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-quotient-nonzerodivisor] gives the pure-codimension-$r$ equality required by [def-pur-frame-class]. Thus the coordinate class $\alpha_U=\partial\kappa(x_1)\cup\cdots\cup\partial\kappa(x_r)$ is defined for this smooth pair, even when $T$ is singular. The vanishing statement of [lem-pur-relative-support-bottom-descent], applied with $B=U$, says $\mathcal H^q_{z(U)}(A(r))=0$ for $q<2r$ on $E_U$.

source.place: Step 3 corrected: use the zero section rather than the zero scheme of an arbitrary section

proof.text: The local vanishing of Step 2 makes $\mathcal H^q_{z(T)}(A(r))=0$ on $E$ for $q<2r$, since a sheaf is zero if its restrictions to an open cover are zero. By [lem-pur-supported-bottom-gluing], $H^{2r}_{z(T)}(E,A(r))$ is the sections of its degree-$2r$ local-cohomology sheaf, compatibly with the finite etale/pro-etale comparison. On an overlap, the two coordinate tuples frame the same ideal in the smooth pair $E\to T$, $z(T)\to T$. By [lem-pur-frame-independence] their classes agree. The sheaf axiom, through the cited edge isomorphism, therefore gives a unique class $u_F\in H^{2r}_{z(T)}(E,A(r))$ with these local coordinate values. This is the only gluing used to construct the localized class; its semi-purity hypothesis has just been proved on $E$.

source.place: Step 3 corrected: valid lowest-degree gluing on the total space

proof.text: For $g:T'\to T$, write $h:E(g^*F)\to E(F)$. The supported pullback of [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality] takes each coordinate boundary on $E_U$ to the same coordinate boundary on $E(g^*F)_{U'}$ and preserves the product. Both $h^*u_F$ and $u_{g^*F}$ thus have the prescribed coordinate values on the inverse-image cover. Apply [lem-pur-supported-bottom-gluing] on the new total space, where [lem-pur-relative-support-bottom-descent] applies with base $T'$ as in Step 2. It gives the global equality $h^*u_F=u_{g^*F}$. No smoothness of $T'$ over $k$ or of an arbitrary section's zero locus has been used.

source.place: Step 3 and Step 4 (L2): equality checked only on the semi-pure universal pair

proof.text: Now let $s:T\to E(F)$ be the given section [def-pur-regular-section]. Define $c_r(F,s)=s^*u_F$ using [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality]. Its support is exactly $T\times_{E(F)}z(T)=Z(s)$ by the definition of the zero scheme. By [lem-pur-supported-hom] it is the displayed morphism $i_*A_{Z(s)}\to A_T(r)[2r]$. This constructs a single global class by pullback; it makes no gluing claim about $H^{2r}_{Z(s)}(-,A(r))$. The construction in fact makes sense for every section; the assertion here uses it on the specified regular sections.

source.place: Step 3: global construction replacing invalid descent on the zero locus

proof.text: For a line bundle $F$, $z(T)\subset E(F)$ is the zero divisor of the tautological section of $\pi^*F$; locally it is $x=0$ in $\mathbf A^1_U$, an effective Cartier divisor. Apply [lem-pur-divisor-class] to the smooth pair $E(F)\to T$, $z(T)\to T$: its class $\operatorname{cl}(z(T))$ has local values $\partial\kappa(x)$, so it equals $u_F$ globally by [lem-pur-supported-bottom-gluing] (vanishing as in Step 3). Since $s$ is regular [def-pur-regular-section], at each $t\in Z(s)$ its local component is a nonzerodivisor of the Noetherian ring $\mathcal O_{T,t}$, hence on a neighbourhood (the kernel of multiplication is coherent and its support misses $Z(s)$), and off $Z(s)$ the ideal is the unit ideal; so $Z(s)=s^{-1}(z(T))$ is an effective Cartier divisor of $T$. The pullback clause of [lem-pur-cartier-class-agreement] for $h=s$ gives $c_1(F,s)=s^*u_F=s^*\operatorname{cl}(z(T))=\operatorname{cl}(Z(s))$, the localized Kummer class of the Cartier divisor of $s$ in the general Cartier construction of [lem-pur-divisor-class] (with base $T$). This proves (L1) for arbitrary $T$, without smoothness of $Z(s)$ over $k$ and without gluing on the pair $(T,Z(s))$.

source.place: Step 4 (L1), with the smooth-pair hypothesis used only for the universal divisor

proof.text:
For $g:T'\to T$ let $s'$ denote the pulled-back section and $h:E(g^*F)\to E(F)$. The equality of scheme maps $s\circ g=h\circ s'$ and composition compatibility of supported pullback give
$$g^*c_r(F,s)=g^*s^*u_F=s'^*h^*u_F=s'^*u_{g^*F}=c_r(g^*F,s').$$
This proves (L2) whenever $s'$ is regular. For a tautological section the components remain polynomial variables after any allowed base change, so regularity is preserved, including over singular bases.

On $E(F\oplus G)=E(F)\times_TE(G)$, let $v_F,v_G$ be the projections. The product $v_F^*u_F\cup v_G^*u_G$ is supported on the intersection of the inverse-image zero sections, exactly the zero section of $F\oplus G$. On a simultaneous trivialization it is the ordered product of all the coordinate Kummer boundaries. By associativity in [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality] this is the local value defining $u_{F\oplus G}$. The bottom-degree gluing lemma applies on this total space by Step 2 and makes the two global classes equal. Pull this global equality back along $(s,t):T\to E(F\oplus G)$. Pullback preserves the internal cup product, so it gives $c_{r+e}(F\oplus G,(s,t))=c_r(F,s)\cup c_e(G,t)$ on the scheme-theoretic intersection of supports. Under the transversality hypothesis [def-pur-regular-section], all three sections belong to the statement. This proves (L3) without an exterior Kunneth formula over $k$.

source.place: Step 4 (L3): internal product on the common base

proof.text: For (L4) pull $F$ back to $p:S=\operatorname{Fl}_T(F)\to T$. Let $0=F_0\subset\cdots\subset F_r=p^*F$ and $Q_j=F_j/F_{j-1}$ be the actual tautological filtration. On the nested total subbundles $E_j=E(F_j)$ form the composite $\Theta_r$ of the Cartier maps $E_{j-1}\hookrightarrow E_j$ in [lem-pur-flag-localized-product]. Locally on $S$ choose an adapted frame by successively splitting the surjections onto the free rank-one quotients. In that frame the chain is $\mathbf A^0\subset\cdots\subset\mathbf A^r$. By [lem-pur-flag-local-comparison], $\Theta_r$ is its coordinate supported product, hence the local value of $u_{p^*F}$. These are classes on the full total space $E(p^*F)$ supported on its zero section. Step 2 gives semi-purity there, so [lem-pur-supported-bottom-gluing] proves $\Theta_r=u_{p^*F}$ globally. Intermediate zero loci of arbitrary sections are never used.

source.place: Steps 2–3 repaired: filtered total-space product and valid global comparison

proof.text:
Write $\pi_S:E(p^*F)\to S$. Forgetting the support of the equality in Step 9, [lem-pur-flag-localized-product] gives
$$\operatorname{forg}(u_{p^*F})=\pi_S^*\prod_{j=1}^r c_{1,A}(Q_j).$$
By Step 4, supported base change identifies the pullback of $u_F$ with $u_{p^*F}$. Pull back the displayed ordinary equality along the pulled-back section $s_S:S\to E(p^*F)$. Since $\pi_Ss_S=\operatorname{id}_S$ and forgetting support commutes with pullback [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality], this gives
$$p^*\operatorname{forg}(c_r(F,s))=\prod_{j=1}^r c_{1,A}(Q_j).$$

source.place: Step 4 (L4): support-forgetting calculation on the flag bundle

proof.text: Ordinary Chern classes are defined by the projective-bundle relation [def-pur-chern-classes], independently of this construction. Pulling that relation back along a morphism gives the relation of the pulled-back bundle: the hyperplane class is natural [lem-pur-kummer-additivity], and the projective-bundle basis is compatible with base change [thm-pur-projective-bundle-formula]. Uniqueness of coefficients therefore gives $p^*c_r(F)=c_r(p^*F)$. Apply [lem-pur-chern-flag-formula] to its filtration to identify this with $\prod_j c_{1,A}(Q_j)$. Step 10 gives the same expression for $p^*\operatorname{forg}(c_r(F,s))$. Finally [lem-pur-flag-pullback-injective] with full support implies $\operatorname{forg}(c_r(F,s))=c_r(F)$ on $T$. This proves (L4). All class construction and comparisons used ordinary cohomology with support and the projective-bundle splitting principle; no exceptional purity or derived-object descent is assumed.

source.place: Step 4 (L4): ordinary splitting principle and injectivity

blueprint_update.statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $F$ be a rank-$r$ vector bundle on $T$, let $s$ be a regular
section, and write $i:Z(s)\hookrightarrow T$. There is a canonical
morphism

$$
c_r(F,s):i_*\Lambda_{Z(s)}\longrightarrow\Lambda_T(r)[2r]
$$

with the following properties:

1. *(L1)* for $r=1$ it is the localized Kummer class of the
Cartier divisor of $s$ (of [lem-pur-divisor-class]);
1. *(L2)* it commutes with base change whenever the
pulled-back section is still regular, in particular with
arbitrary base change for the tautological section on the total
space of a vector bundle;
1. *(L3)* for a transverse direct sum of sections it is the
cup product of the two localized classes;
1. *(L4)* after forgetting support it is $c_r(F)$.

proof.text:
The line-bundle class in the proposed construction is the divisor class of [lem-pur-divisor-class]; products have their twists identified by [def-coefficient-twists-detailed].
Step 1: the flag-bundle pullback is injective. Write the group in
the form

$$
H^{2r}_{Z(s)}(T,\Lambda(r))
:=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(T,\Lambda)}
\bigl(i_*\Lambda_{Z(s)},\Lambda_T(r)[2r]\bigr).
$$

Pull $F$ back to its complete flag bundle $p:T'\to T$. Iterating
[thm-pur-projective-bundle-formula] gives a direct-sum
decomposition of $Rp_*\Lambda_{T'}$ whose degree-zero summand is
$\Lambda_T$; projection to this summand with the projection formula
is a left inverse to

$$
p^*:H^{2r}_{Z(s)}(T,\Lambda(r))
\longrightarrow
H^{2r}_{Z(s)\times_TT'}(T',\Lambda(r)),
$$

so this pullback is injective: the ordinary splitting principle for the
displayed abelian group.

Step 2: the class on the flag bundle. On $T'$ the flag quotients are
line bundles; successively take the localized Kummer classes of the
induced line-bundle sections on their successive zero loci and cup them,
obtaining an element
$\operatorname{cl}_{T'}\in H^{2r}_{Z(s)\times_TT'}(T',\Lambda(r))$.
The result is unchanged under a refinement of the flag: expanding the
product and using the additivity of
[lem-pur-kummer-additivity]
($c_1(L\otimes M)=c_1(L)+c_1(M)$) shows that it is the symmetric
elementary polynomial of degree $r$ in the Chern roots.

Step 3: the class descends, by localizing on the base. The following
gives a well-defined class on every open $T_0\subseteq T$ over which $F$
is trivial, and it is here that the descent is justified — by
[lem-pur-frame-independence], not by the degree-zero summand of the
projective-bundle decomposition. Choose an isomorphism
$F|_{T_0}\cong\mathcal O_{T_0}^r$ and write
$s|_{T_0}=(s_1,\dots,s_r)$ with $s_i\in\Gamma(T_0,\mathcal O)$; the
regularity of $s$ says exactly that $s_1,\dots,s_r$ is a frame of the
ideal of $Z(s)$ in the sense of [def-pur-frame-class], so put

$$
c_r(F,s)|_{T_0}=\kappa(s_1)\cup\cdots\cup\kappa(s_r)
\in H^{2r}_{Z(s)}(T_0,\Lambda(r)).
$$

A second trivialization is related to the first by an invertible matrix over
$T_0$, so by [lem-pur-frame-independence] the class depends only on
the ideal of $Z(s)$, hence only on the open and on $s$; on an overlap
the two frames frame the same ideal, so the classes agree and glue, and
because $H^{2r}_{Z(s)}(-,\Lambda(r))$ is computed by the sheaf-theoretic
operations of [def-pur-support-cohomology] they give an element
$c_r(F,s)\in H^{2r}_{Z(s)}(T,\Lambda(r))$. Now compare with
$\operatorname{cl}_{T'}$. Over a trivializing open $T_0$ the flag
bundle is $T_0\times_kG/B$, and there the universal filtration of the
trivialized bundle has line quotients whose sections are the images of the
components $s_i$ of the frame; the zero locus of such a section is the
preimage of $V(s_i)$, so by the functoriality of the Kummer class and of
the supported product the successive construction of Step 2 restricts to
the pullback of $\kappa(s_1)\cup\cdots\cup\kappa(s_r)$, that is, to
$p^*(c_r(F,s)|_{T_0})$. The trivializing opens cover $T$, so
$p^*c_r(F,s)=\operatorname{cl}_{T'}$. In particular the class of Step 2
does lie in the image of the injective pullback $p^*$ of Step 1, which is
what had to be shown, and $c_r(F,s)$ is the unique element with that
pullback.

Step 4: the four properties. They follow after the injective
flag-bundle pullback, where they reduce respectively to the rank-one
Kummer construction, the functoriality of a local equation, the
associativity and direct-sum behaviour of the cup product (with the
transversality as in [lem-pur-kunneth-supported]), and the usual
splitting-principle definition of $c_r(F)$. This is descent of one
element along a split injection of abelian groups, not descent of
derived categories or derived objects.
